Use base × height ÷ 2: 10 × 6 ÷ 2.

items.prompt: What is the size of each angle inside a regular octagon?

figure.alt: A regular octagon: 8 equal sides and 8 equal angles.

options.why: 108° is the angle in a regular pentagon.
120° is the angle in a regular hexagon.
140° is the angle in a regular 9-sided shape.
144° is the angle in a regular 10-sided shape.

hints: Split the octagon into triangles from one corner.
From one corner, an octagon splits into 6 triangles.
The angles add up to 6 × 180°.
items.explanation: From one corner an octagon splits into 6 triangles, so its angles add up to 6 × 180° = 1080°. Each of the 8 equal angles is 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°.

items.prompt: A square fits exactly inside a circle, with its 4 corners on the circle. The circle has a radius of 5 cm. What is the area of the square?

figure.alt: A circle with a radius of 5 cm. A square sits inside it with all 4 corners touching the circle.

options.why: 25 cm² is a square with sides of 5 cm. Here the diagonal is 10 cm.
Split the square into 4 triangles from the centre.
78.5 cm² is roughly the area of the circle, not the square.
100 cm² is the square around the outside of the circle.

hints: The diagonals of the square are diameters of the circle.
Each diagonal is 10 cm long, and the diagonals cross at the centre.
Cut the square into 4 triangles along its diagonals.
items.explanation: The diagonals cut the square into 4 right-angled triangles, each with two sides of 5 cm. Each triangle has an area of 5 × 5 ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm², so the square is 4 × 12.5 = 50 cm².

solution.say: 4 triangles with two sides of 5 cm.

items.prompt: A 6 × 4 × 3 cuboid is built from 1 cm cubes and painted on the outside. How many small cubes have exactly one painted face?

figure.alt: A cuboid 6 cubes long, 4 cubes wide and 3 cubes tall, made of 1 cm cubes and painted on the outside.

hints: Cubes with one painted face are in the middle of a face, away from every edge.
On a face of 6 by 4, the middle part is 4 by 2.
Do the same for the 6 by 3 and 4 by 3 faces. There are two of each face.
items.explanation: The middle parts are 4 × 2 = 8 on each 6 × 4 face, 4 × 1 = 4 on each 6 × 3 face and 2 × 1 = 2 on each 4 × 3 face. With two of each face: 2 × (8 + 4 + 2) = 28.

items.prompt: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the size of the largest angle?
hints: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The ratio has 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts.
Find the size of one part.
items.explanation: There are 9 parts, so one part is 180° ÷ 9 = 20°. The largest angle is 4 parts: 80°.

items.prompt: ABCDE is a regular pentagon. What is the size of angle ABD, between the side BA and the diagonal BD?

figure.alt: A regular pentagon with corners A, B, C, D and E in order. A diagonal joins B to D.

hints: Each angle of a regular pentagon is 108°.
Triangle BCD has BC = CD, so its two base angles are equal.
items.explanation: Each angle of the pentagon is 108°. In triangle BCD, BC = CD and angle C = 108°, so angle CBD = (180° - 108°) ÷ 2 = 36°. Then angle ABD = 108° - 36° = 72°.

items.prompt: On a grid, A is at (1, 1), B is at (7, 1) and C is at (4, 5). What is the area of triangle ABC in square units?

figure.alt: A grid with points A at (1, 1), B at (7, 1) and C at (4, 5), joined to make a triangle.

hints: Use AB as the base.
AB is flat, from x = 1 to x = 7.
The height is how far C is above the line AB.
items.explanation: The base AB is 7 - 1 = 6 units long. C is 5 - 1 = 4 units above AB, so the height is 4. The area is 6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 square units.

items.prompt: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 cm. Its length is twice its width. What is its area in square centimetres?
hints: Half of the perimeter is length plus width.
Half of 36 is 18. Length is 2 parts and width is 1 part.
The width is 6 cm.
items.explanation: Length plus width is 18 cm. The width is 6 cm and the length is 12 cm. The area is 12 × 6 = 72 cm².

items.prompt: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:30? Give your answer in degrees.
hints: The minute hand points to 6 at half past.
The hour hand is half-way between 4 and 5.
Each hour mark is 30° apart.
items.explanation: At 4:30 the minute hand is at 180°. The hour hand has moved 4.5 hours, which is 4.5 × 30 = 135°. The difference is 45°.

items.prompt: A square has side 10 cm. A small triangle with two sides of 3 cm at right angles is cut off each corner. What is the area left, in square centimetres?
hints: Find the area of one cut-off triangle.
It has area 3 × 3 ÷ 2 = 4.5.
There are 4 corners.
items.explanation: Each triangle has area 3 × 3 ÷ 2 = 4.5. Four of them make 18. So 100 − 18 = 82 cm².

items.prompt: A cube has a volume of 125 cubic centimetres. What is its total surface area in square centimetres?
hints: Find the side length of the cube.
What number multiplied by itself three times is 125?
The side is 5 cm. A cube has 6 faces.
items.explanation: The side is 5 cm because 5 × 5 × 5 = 125. Each face has area 25 cm² and there are 6 faces. 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

items.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle A is 60°. Angle B is 4 times as big as angle C. What is the size of angle B in degrees?
hints: The three angles add up to 180°.
Angles B and C together are 180 − 60 = 120.
B is 4 parts and C is 1 part, so 5 parts make 120°.
items.explanation: B + C = 120°. In 5 equal parts, one part is 24°, so C = 24° and B = 4 × 24 = 96°.

items.prompt: A square of side 12 cm is cut into 3 rectangles by two straight cuts, both parallel to one side. What is the total perimeter of the 3 rectangles together, in centimetres?
hints: Start with the perimeter of the whole square.
Each cut is 12 cm long and creates two new edges, one for each piece.
There are two cuts.
items.explanation: The square has perimeter 48 cm. Each cut is 12 cm and makes two new edges, adding 24 cm. Two cuts add 48 cm. The total is 48 + 48 = 96 cm.

options.why: This is the perimeter of the square only. The cuts make new edges.
You added one cut. There are two cuts, and each cut makes two new edges.
You counted each cut as adding 3 edges. Each cut adds two edges of 12 cm.

items.prompt: The three different faces of a cuboid have areas 12 cm², 15 cm² and 20 cm². What is the volume of the cuboid in cubic centimetres?
hints: Call the edges a, b and c. The face areas are ab, bc and ac.
Multiplying all three areas gives (abc) × (abc).
12 × 15 × 20 = 3,600. What number times itself is 3,600?
items.explanation: Multiplying the three face areas gives (abc)², which is 12 × 15 × 20 = 3,600. So the volume abc is √3,600 = 60 cm³. (The edges are 3, 4 and 5.)

items.prompt: On a coordinate grid, the corners of a triangle are P(−3, −2), Q(7, 0) and R(1, 6). What is the area of the triangle in square units?
hints: Draw a rectangle round the triangle, with sides parallel to the axes.
The rectangle goes from x = −3 to 7 and y = −2 to 6, so it is 10 by 8.
Take away the three corner triangles.
items.explanation: The rectangle is 10 by 8 = 80. The three corner triangles have areas 10 × 2 ÷ 2 = 10, 6 × 6 ÷ 2 = 18 and 4 × 8 ÷ 2 = 16. So the area is 80 − 10 − 18 − 16 = 36.
